description: Mentalist is an independent team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026  We combine technology artificial intelligence  data science, and creativity to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Our focus is on using NASA Earth observation data to explore smarter agricultural strategies improve soil health, conserve water and strengthen climate resilience We believe in teamwork scientific thinking and turning data into meaningful impact.
summary: Hassouna Green is a bilingual interactive 3D farming prototype built for the Field Shift challenge It addresses the difficulty of planning crop rotations when climate conditions and water availability change Users can explore planting and water management in an educational farm simulation and compare different crop sequences across seasons based on their priorities NASA POWER weather records provide environmental context while crop comparisons use transparent simplified rules The prototype makes agricultural tradeoffs easier to understand and shows why looking beyond one season matters for soil health and farm resilience It is a learning and exploration tool rather than a validated agricultural recommendation system and provides a foundation for future decision support using local field data and agronomist guidance.
details:
• Hassouna Green is an interactive 3D farm prototype in Arabic and English built by Team Mentalist for the Field Shift challenge to help users plan crop rotations across several seasons
  • Users pick Cairo or the Nile Delta and choose a priority and a starting rotation and then plant and water and add soil cover and harvest during a 12-day demo season
  • The Compare crop rotations panel shows the user's rotation next to a diversified option and a soil-focused option and a lower-water option with simple water and diversity scores
  • A Node JS handler requests daily NASA POWER weather data and the game falls back to a labelled 2025 NASA POWER archive for Cairo and the Nile Delta when live data is not available
  • Daily temperature and rainfall drive simple game rules for moisture and crop growth while a SoilGrids example for the Nile Delta is included only as background
  • The rotation scores come from open rules we wrote ourselves based on crop water needs and diversity and legumes and do not use NASA or SoilGrids values
  • Working now are the bilingual 3D demo and the rotation comparison and the season report and progress saved in the browser and public code that judges can open without logging in
  • It is not yet a validated recommendation system and does not predict yield or income or irrigation needs and it has no farmer feedback backend or field trials
  • Future plans are local soil and field data and agronomist-calibrated models and a farmer feedback loop and more NASA datasets and field trials with farmers
  • Built with HTML and CSS and JavaScript and Three JS and Node JS and VS Code with the public demo hosted on Manus and no special hardware needed beyond a browser that supports WebGL.
